CSCO.rationale: Cisco's business trajectory is genuinely strong: Q3 FY2026 revenue of $15.84B (+12% YoY) beat consensus, product orders surged 35% YoY (50%+ in networking), AI infrastructure orders reached $5.3B YTD with the FY2026 target raised to $9B, and operating margin expanded to 24.6% from 22.2% YoY. The franchise is high-quality with ~43% global Ethernet switching share and 98-99% Fortune 500 penetration. However, the stock has re-rated so aggressively — PE from 28x to 41.6x (top of 365-day range), P/B from 5.65x to 9.65x — that it now prices in near-perfection. The earnings yield of 2.4% sits 207bps below the 10-year Treasury at 4.47%, creating a historically unusual negative spread for a mature infrastructure company. Operating cash flow declined 43.3% QoQ to $1.82B against $3.17B net income, flagging earnings-quality concerns. Non-GAAP gross margin compressed to 66.0% from 68.6% YoY due to memory costs and tariffs, with Q4 guidance of 65.5-66.5% suggesting persistence. Security revenue was flat at ~$2B despite the $28B Splunk investment. The Q3 blowout and AI momentum are real positive catalysts (pillar 3), but the stock's 54% quarterly surge has already captured much of this — the 13-18% post-earnings pop on May 14 means the re-rating catalyst is largely priced. Net: excellent franchise with improving trajectory, but valuation at 365-day extremes with rising rates and OCF weakness caps the score modestly above neutral.
